questions.stem: The function \(f(x) = 206(1.034)^x\) models the value, in dollars, of a certain bank account by the end of each year from 1957 through 1972, where \(x\) is the number of years after 1957. Which of the following is the best interpretation of "\(f(5)\) is approximately equal to 243" in this context?
options: The value of the bank account is estimated to be approximately 5 dollars greater in 1962 than in 1957.
The value of the bank account is estimated to be approximately 243 dollars in 1962.
The value, in dollars, of the bank account is estimated to be approximately 5 times greater in 1962 than in 1957.
The value of the bank account is estimated to increase by approximately 243 dollars every 5 years between 1957 and 1972.
questions.explanation: \(x = 5\) corresponds to 5 years after 1957, which is 1962, and \(f(5) \approx 243\) means the account value is about 243 dollars in 1962.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 270(0.1)^x\). What is the value of \(f(0)\)?

\(f(x) = 5{,}470(0.64)^{\frac{x}{12}}\) The function \(f\) gives the value, in dollars, of a certain piece of equipment after \(x\) months of use. If the value of the equipment decreases each year by \(p\%\) of its value the preceding year, what is the value of \(p\)?
questions.explanation: Over one year (12 months), the factor is \((0.64)^{\frac{12}{12}} = 0.64\), so the value is 64% of the previous year, a decrease of \(100 - 64 = 36\%\). Thus \(p = 36\).

questions.stem: Which of the following functions has(have) a minimum value at \(-3\)? I. \(f(x) = -6(3)^x - 3\) II. \(g(x) = -3(6)^x\)
questions.explanation: Both functions have a negative leading coefficient multiplying a growing exponential, so each decreases without bound (no minimum). Function I approaches \(-3\) as an asymptote from below but never reaches a minimum; function II approaches 0 from below. Neither attains a minimum value of \(-3\).

questions.stem: \(P(t) = 260(1.04)^{\left(\frac{6}{4}\right)t}\) The function \(P\) models the population, in thousands, of a certain city \(t\) years after 2003. According to the model, the population is predicted to increase by 4% every \(n\) months. What is the value of \(n\)?
questions.explanation: The base 1.04 (a 4% increase) applies when the exponent \(\frac{6}{4}t = 1\), i.e. \(t = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}\) years. Converting to months: \(\frac{2}{3} \times 12 = 8\) months.

questions.stem: \(P(t) = 1{,}800(1.02)^t\) The function \(P\) gives the estimated number of marine mammals in a certain area, where \(t\) is the number of years since a study began. What is the best interpretation of \(P(0) = 1{,}800\) in this context?
options: The estimated number of marine mammals in the area was 102 when the study began.
The estimated number of marine mammals in the area was 1,800 when the study began.
The estimated number of marine mammals in the area increased by 102 each year during the study.
The estimated number of marine mammals in the area increased by 1,800 each year during the study.
questions.explanation: At \(t = 0\) (when the study began), \(P(0) = 1{,}800\), so there were an estimated 1,800 marine mammals at the start.

questions.stem: At the time that an article was first featured on the home page of a news website, there were 40 comments on the article. An exponential model estimates that at the end of each hour after the article was first featured on the home page, the number of comments on the article had increased by 190% of the number of comments on the article at the end of the previous hour. Which of the following equations best represents this model, where \(C\) is the estimated number of comments on the article \(t\) hours after the article was first featured on the home page and \(t \le 4\)?
questions.explanation: An increase of 190% each hour means the new amount is the previous amount plus 1.9 times it, a factor of \(1 + 1.9 = 2.9\). So \(C = 40(2.9)^t\).

questions.stem: \(f(x) = (1.84)^{\frac{x}{4}}\) The function \(f\) is defined by the given equation. The equation can be rewritten as \(f(x) = \left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)^x\), where \(p\) is a constant. Which of the following is closest to the value of \(p\)?

For the exponential function \(f\), the value of \(f(0)\) is \(c\), where \(c\) is a constant. Of the following equations that define the function \(f\), which equation shows the value of \(c\) as the coefficient or the base?
questions.explanation: \(f(0) = c\). For \(f(x) = 33(1.5)^x\), \(f(0) = 33\), so \(c = 33\) appears directly as the coefficient.

questions.stem: The function \(f(t) = 40{,}000(2)^{\frac{t}{790}}\) gives the number of bacteria in a population \(t\) minutes after an initial observation. How much time, in minutes, does it take for the number of bacteria in the population to double?
questions.explanation: The population doubles when the exponent \(\frac{t}{790} = 1\), i.e. \(t = 790\) minutes.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{h^{15}q^7}{h^5 q^{21}}\), where \(h > 0\) and \(q > 0\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract exponents for like bases: \(h^{15-5} = h^{10}\) and \(q^{7-21} = q^{-14}\). So the expression is \(\frac{h^{10}}{q^{14}}\).

questions.stem: The graph shown is an increasing exponential curve that approaches the \(x\)-axis on the left and crosses the \(y\)-axis at 8. What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph shown?
questions.explanation: The \(y\)-intercept is where the curve crosses the \(y\)-axis, which occurs at \((0, 8)\).

questions.stem: A model predicts that the population of Bergen was 15,000 in 2005. The model also predicts that each year for the next 5 years, the population \(p\) increased by 4% of the previous year's population. Which equation best represents this model, where \(x\) is the number of years after 2005, for \(x \le 5\)?
questions.explanation: A 4% annual increase gives a growth factor of \(1.04\), starting from 15,000: \(p = 15{,}000(1.04)^x\).

questions.stem: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by the given equations, where \(x \ge 0\). Which of the following equations displays, as a constant or coefficient, the maximum value of the function it defines, where \(x \ge 0\)? I. \(f(x) = 18(1.25)^x + 41\) II. \(g(x) = 9(0.73)^x\)
questions.explanation: For \(g(x) = 9(0.73)^x\) with base less than 1, the function decreases, so its maximum at \(x = 0\) is \(9\), which appears as the coefficient. For \(f(x) = 18(1.25)^x + 41\), the base exceeds 1, so the function increases without bound and has no maximum. Only II displays its maximum.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(a^{\frac{11}{12}}\), where \(a > 0\)?

A company opens an account with an initial balance of 36,100.00 dollars. The account earns interest, and no additional deposits or withdrawals are made. The account balance is given by an exponential function \(A\), where \(A(t)\) is the account balance, in dollars, \(t\) years after the account is opened. The account balance after 13 years is 68,071.93 dollars. Which equation could define \(A\)?
questions.explanation: The initial balance at \(t = 0\) must be 36,100.00, which rules out the options starting at 31,971.93. A growth factor of 1.05 gives \(36{,}100(1.05)^{13} \approx 68{,}072\), matching the given balance, so \(A(t) = 36{,}100.00(1.05)^t\).

questions.stem: For \(x > 0\), the function \(f\) is defined as follows: \(f(x)\) equals 201% of \(x\). Which of the following could describe this function?
questions.explanation: \(f(x) = 2.01x\) is a linear function with positive slope, so it is increasing linear.

questions.stem: Rosa opened a savings account at a bank. A table shows the exponential relationship between the time \(t\), in years, since Rosa opened the account and the total amount \(n\), in dollars, in the account: at \(t = 0\), \(n = 604.00\); at \(t = 1\), \(n = 606.42\); at \(t = 2\), \(n = 608.84\). If Rosa made no additional deposits or withdrawals, which of the following equations best represents the relationship between \(t\) and \(n\)?
questions.explanation: The initial amount at \(t = 0\) is 604. The yearly growth factor is \(\frac{606.42}{604} \approx 1.004\), a 0.4% increase. So \(n = 604(1 + 0.004)^t\).

questions.stem: The population of Greenville increased by 7% from 2015 to 2016. If the 2016 population is \(k\) times the 2015 population, what is the value of \(k\)?
questions.explanation: A 7% increase multiplies the population by \(1 + 0.07 = 1.07\), so \(k = 1.07\).

questions.stem: \(m(t) = -0.0274\left(\frac{t}{7}\right)^2 + 7.3873\left(\frac{t}{7}\right) + 75.032\) The function \(m\) gives the predicted body mass \(m(t)\), in kilograms (kg), of a certain animal \(t\) days after it was born in a wildlife reserve, where \(t \le 390\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of the statement "\(m(330)\) is approximately equal to 362" in this context?
options: The predicted body mass of the animal was approximately 330 kg 362 days after it was born.
The predicted body mass of the animal was approximately 362 kg 330 days after it was born.
The predicted body mass of the animal was approximately 362 times 330 divided by 7 days after it was born.
The predicted body mass of the animal was approximately 330 divided by 7 kg 362 days after it was born.
questions.explanation: In \(m(t)\), the input \(t\) is days and the output is body mass in kg. So \(m(330) \approx 362\) means the predicted body mass was about 362 kg when the animal was 330 days old.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = a(2.2^x + 2.2^b)\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are integer constants and \(0 < a < b\). The functions \(g\) and \(h\) are equivalent to function \(f\), where \(k\) and \(m\) are constants. Which of the following equations displays the \(y\)-coordinate of the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane as a constant or coefficient? I. \(g(x) = a(2.2^x + k)\) II. \(h(x) = a(2.2)^x + m\)
questions.explanation: The \(y\)-intercept is \(f(0) = a(2.2^0 + 2.2^b) = a(1 + 2.2^b)\). In form I, \(g(x) = a(2.2^x + k)\) has \(g(0) = a(1 + k)\), so the intercept value \(a(1+k)\) is not shown as a standalone constant. In form II, \(h(x) = a(2.2)^x + m\) has \(h(0) = a + m\), which also does not display the full intercept as a single constant. Neither displays it directly.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((m^4 q^4 z^{-1})(m q^5 z^3)\), where \(m\), \(q\), and \(z\) are positive?
questions.explanation: Add exponents of like bases: \(m^{4+1} q^{4+5} z^{-1+3} = m^5 q^9 z^2\).

questions.stem: An airplane descends from an altitude of 9,500 feet to 5,000 feet at a constant rate of 400 feet per minute. What type of function best models the relationship between the descending airplane's altitude and time?
questions.explanation: A constant rate of descent means altitude decreases by a fixed amount each minute, which is a decreasing linear function.

questions.stem: The number of bacteria in a liquid medium doubles every day. There are 44,000 bacteria in the liquid medium at the start of an observation. Which of the following represents the number of bacteria, \(y\), in the liquid medium \(t\) days after the start of the observation?
questions.explanation: Starting at 44,000 and doubling each day gives a growth factor of 2: \(y = 44{,}000(2)^t\).

questions.stem: A table shows the exponential relationship between the number of years, \(x\), since Hana started training in pole vault, and the estimated height \(h(x)\), in meters, of her best pole vault for that year: at \(x = 0\), \(h(x) = 1.23\); at \(x = 2\), \(h(x) = 1.54\); at \(x = 4\), \(h(x) = 1.94\). Which of the following functions best represents this relationship, where \(x \le 4\)?
questions.explanation: At \(x = 0\), the value is 1.23, which is the coefficient. Over 2 years the height grows by a factor of \(\frac{1.54}{1.23} \approx 1.252\), so the yearly factor is \(\sqrt{1.252} \approx 1.12\). Thus \(h(x) = 1.23(1.12)^x\).

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = (-8)(2)^x + 22\). What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane?

For the exponential function \(f\), the value of \(f(1)\) is \(k\), where \(k\) is a constant. Which of the following equivalent forms of the function \(f\) shows the value of \(k\) as the coefficient or the base?
questions.explanation: We need the form where evaluating at \(x = 1\) makes the exponent 0, leaving the coefficient as \(f(1)\). In \(f(x) = 128(1.6)^{x-1}\), \(f(1) = 128(1.6)^0 = 128 = k\), so \(k\) appears directly as the coefficient.

questions.stem: There are 240 players in a tennis competition that includes 4 rounds of matches. Each player in the competition will play a match against another player in round 1. At the end of each round, the player who loses the match is eliminated and the player who won the match advances to the next round to play a match against another winning player. Which equation gives the number of players, \(p\), eliminated at the end of round \(r\), where \(r \le 4\)?
questions.explanation: Each round eliminates half the players remaining. Starting from 240, the number eliminated at the end of round \(r\) is \(p = 240\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^r\).

questions.stem: Evaluate \(2^5\).
questions.explanation: \(2^5 = 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 32\).

questions.stem: Evaluate \(3^4\).
Evaluate \(5^3\).
If \(f(x) = 3 \cdot 2^x\), what is \(f(2)\)?
If \(f(x) = 5 \cdot 2^x\), what is the initial value \(f(0)\)?
questions.explanation: Any nonzero base to the \(0\) power is \(1\), so \(f(0) = 5 \cdot 1 = 5\).

questions.stem: In the model \(y = 100 \cdot (1.05)^x\), is this growth or decay?
questions.explanation: The base \(1.05 > 1\), so the quantity grows.

questions.stem: In the model \(y = 200 \cdot (0.9)^x\), is this growth or decay?
questions.explanation: The base \(0.9 < 1\), so the quantity decays.

questions.stem: A population increases by \(6\%\) each year. What is the growth factor?
questions.explanation: A \(6\%\) increase multiplies by \(1 + 0.06 = 1.06\) each year.

questions.stem: A quantity decreases by \(15\%\) each year. What is the decay factor?
questions.explanation: A \(15\%\) decrease multiplies by \(1 - 0.15 = 0.85\) each year.

questions.stem: Simplify \(x^3 \cdot x^4\).
questions.explanation: When multiplying like bases, add exponents: \(x^{3+4} = x^7\).

questions.stem: Simplify \((x^2)^5\).
questions.explanation: A power raised to a power multiplies exponents: \(x^{2 \cdot 5} = x^{10}\).

questions.stem: Evaluate \(2^{-3}\).
questions.explanation: A negative exponent is a reciprocal: \(2^{-3} = \tfrac{1}{2^3} = \tfrac18\).

questions.stem: Evaluate \(7^0\).
questions.explanation: Any nonzero number to the \(0\) power equals \(1\).

questions.stem: A bacteria colony doubles every hour, starting at \(50\). How many are there after \(3\) hours?
questions.explanation: After \(3\) doublings: \(50 \cdot 2^3 = 50 \cdot 8 = 400\).

questions.stem: If \(f(x) = 4^x\), what is \(f(3)\)?
Simplify \(\dfrac{x^8}{x^3}\).
questions.explanation: When dividing like bases, subtract exponents: \(x^{8-3} = x^5\).

questions.stem: Write \(0.0003\) in scientific notation.
questions.explanation: Move the decimal \(4\) places right: \(0.0003 = 3 \times 10^{-4}\).

questions.stem: If \(f(x) = 2 \cdot 3^x\), what is \(f(1)\)?
A savings account of \(500\) dollars grows by \(10\%\) in one year. What is the balance after one year, in dollars?
Evaluate \(10^4\).
A car worth \(20{,}000\) dollars loses half its value each year. What is it worth after \(2\) years, in dollars?
questions.explanation: After \(2\) halvings: \(20000 \cdot (\tfrac12)^2 = 20000 \cdot \tfrac14 = 5000\) dollars.

questions.stem: Which base makes \(y = b^x\) an increasing function?
questions.explanation: For \(y = b^x\) to increase, the base must satisfy \(b > 1\); of the choices, only \(3\) qualifies.

questions.stem: Simplify \(x^0 + x^1\) for \(x \neq 0\).
questions.explanation: \(x^0 = 1\) and \(x^1 = x\), so the sum is \(1 + x\).

questions.stem: If \(f(x) = 6 \cdot (\tfrac12)^x\), what is \(f(2)\)?
questions.explanation: \(f(2) = 6 \cdot (\tfrac12)^2 = 6 \cdot \tfrac14 = 1.5\).

questions.stem: A \(3\%\) annual growth is modeled by \(y = P(1 + r)^t\). What is \(r\)?
questions.explanation: The rate as a decimal is \(r = 0.03\).

questions.stem: Evaluate \(4^{1/2}\).
If a value triples every day starting at \(2\), what is it after \(2\) days?
In \(y = 8 \cdot (1.25)^x\), what is the percent growth rate per step?
questions.explanation: The base \(1.25 = 1 + 0.25\), a growth rate of \(25\%\).

questions.stem: An investment of \(1{,}000\) dollars earns \(8\%\) compounded annually. What is its value after \(2\) years, in dollars?
A substance has a half-life of \(3\) years. If \(80\) grams remain now, how much remains after \(9\) years?
questions.explanation: Nine years is \(3\) half-lives: \(80 \cdot (\tfrac12)^3 = 80 \cdot \tfrac18 = 10\) grams.
Since \(32 = 2^5\), we have \(x = 5\).
Since \(81 = 3^4\), we have \(x = 4\).

questions.stem: A population of \(500\) grows \(20\%\) per year. Which function models the population after \(t\) years?
questions.explanation: Growth of \(20\%\) uses a factor of \(1.2\): \(P = 500(1.2)^t\).

questions.stem: A car worth \(24{,}000\) dollars depreciates \(25\%\) per year. What is its value after \(2\) years, in dollars?
The value of \(y = 4 \cdot 2^x\) at \(x = 5\) is what?
An exponential function passes through \((0, 3)\) and \((1, 12)\). What is its base?
questions.explanation: With \(f(0) = 3\) and \(f(1) = 3b = 12\), the base is \(b = 4\).
Subtract exponents: \(2^{10-7} = 2^3 = 8\).

questions.stem: A colony starts at \(64\) and is halved each hour. After how many hours are \(8\) left?
questions.explanation: \(64 \cdot (\tfrac12)^t = 8\) means \((\tfrac12)^t = \tfrac18 = (\tfrac12)^3\), so \(t = 3\).

questions.stem: Which is equivalent to \(9^x\)?
An account grows from \(1{,}000\) to \(1{,}210\) dollars in \(2\) years compounded annually. What is the annual rate?
If \(f(x) = 2^x\), by what factor does \(f\) increase when \(x\) increases by \(3\)?
A tree's height follows \(h = 5 (1.1)^t\) meters. What is its height at \(t = 0\), in meters?
Solve \(4^x = \tfrac{1}{16}\).
A medicine's concentration drops \(30\%\) each hour. What fraction remains after \(3\) hours?
questions.explanation: \((0.7)^3 = 0.343\) of the original remains.

questions.stem: Which grows faster for large \(x\): \(y = 2^x\) or \(y = x^2\)?
questions.explanation: Exponential growth eventually outpaces any polynomial, so \(2^x\) grows faster for large \(x\).
